claims.text: TaVCrW is initially a solid refractory high-entropy alloy with potential short-range order and electronic-gap characteristics at the Fermi level.
An MTP trained on DFT data can replace the EAM reference potential for TaVCrW free-energy calculations.
Free energy perturbation can replace thermodynamic integration for calculating the solid–liquid Gibbs free-energy difference.
The MTP+FEP method will reduce computational cost by more than 80% relative to TOR-TILD.
The MTP+FEP result will remain within 0.5 meV/atom of the TOR-TILD result.
Achieving the stated accuracy requires the MTP to reproduce the ab initio liquid phase-space distribution between 2000 and 2400 K.
Short-range order contributes a stabilization energy of approximately 2–3 meV/atom.
Capturing short-range order and the density of states at the Fermi level is critical for accurate free-energy estimation without thermodynamic integration.
The MTP acts as a computationally efficient surrogate for the DFT energy landscape.
Using the MTP allows FEP to sample phase space directly and bypass the expensive integration steps in TOR-TILD.
Training the MTP to reproduce SRO and the Fermi-level DOS gap will maintain melting-calculation accuracy.
Empirical potentials such as EAM may miss relevant TaVCrW behavior because GGA-PBE/LDA underbinding or overbinding rules fail for V and Cr.
The supercell must be large enough to preserve SRO against artifacts associated with periodic boundaries.
The cited periodic-cell artifact involves destruction of SRO on a slip plane after repeated dislocation passage in high-stress simulations.
The 2000–2400 K range is sufficient to capture liquid stability without phase separation or unmodeled magnetic fluctuations.
Electronic excitations and magnetic fluctuations must be represented in the DFT training data.
High-temperature electronic excitations and magnetic fluctuations may alter the phase-space distribution and cause errors if absent from training.
The reliability of an EAM potential at high temperature cannot be assumed from low-temperature agreement with DFT.
The benchmark should compare MTP+FEP and TOR-TILD on a simpler refractory alloy while varying supercell size and measuring free energy, cost, SRO, and DOS.
The hypothesis is falsified if the MTP+FEP versus TOR-TILD free-energy discrepancy exceeds 0.5 meV/atom or if cost reduction is below 80% at the required accuracy.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome describes a melting-temperature deviation in meV/atom, but meV/atom is an energy unit. The falsification rule instead applies the 0.5 meV/atom threshold to a free-energy discrepancy, so the target observable is inconsistent.

SRO is introduced as a solid-state contribution, but the hypothesis and measurements emphasize capturing SRO in the liquid, while the supercell rationale is imported from slip-plane SRO destruction during dislocation motion. The relevant phase and physical context for the claimed SRO contribution are not consistently specified.
